screens.name: Home — unavailable omen and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 08–09 show a dominant gold orb, explicit touch instruction and unavailable-omen guidance; supplied browser evidence reports enlargement and clearance checks.
findings: Increase the small whisper and helper text slightly while preserving separation from the orb.

screens.name: Home — successful omen fixture
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows the successful omen below the hero with its free label and navigation remaining visible.
findings: Verify longer omen text at enlarged native text sizes without crowding navigation.

screens.name: Approach — loading and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 preserves the orb and opening-status hierarchy across captures, and supplied evidence describes automatic advancement with reduced-motion bypass.
findings: Verify that the brief automatic transition neither interrupts announcements nor leaves focus behind.

screens.name: Ask — normal and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows a labeled question field, voice alternative and distinct submit button with stable transition composition.
findings: Replace the technical phrase “prediction engine” with a plain explanation of where submitted text goes.

screens.name: Ask — enlarged text
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 shows the enlarged question, explanatory text and stacked actions fitting within the captured viewport.
findings: Test longer questions with a physical keyboard open to confirm that submission and question context remain reachable.

screens.name: Listening — voice failure and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 visibly prioritizes typing and explains microphone failure, while supplied evidence states that transcription is preserved.
findings: Place a brief voice-unavailable explanation nearer the typing action so recovery does not depend on noticing the bottom notice.

screens.name: Question card 1 — normal and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows a clear question, four separated choices and progress, with supplied keyboard evidence covering advancement and focus transfer.
findings: Verify native announcement of the next question after immediate answer selection.

screens.name: Question card 2 — normal and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 03 retains the same question and answer alignment across the second-card transition pair.
findings: Confirm that returning to this question exposes the previously chosen answer visually and to assistive technology.

screens.name: Question card 3 — normal and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 03 shows the final question with a 3-of-3 indicator and the same spacious answer rows.
findings: Check whether novices understand that the final answer starts prediction generation immediately.

screens.name: Question card — keyboard-focused heading
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 shows a visible heading focus ring, and supplied keyboard evidence reports that Tab subsequently reaches the first answer.
findings: Give the heading focus ring a little breathing room around the text.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 shows a persistent answer label, Change action, multiline field and visibly disabled Continue button.
findings: Explain that an answer is required before Continue becomes available.

screens.name: Custom answer — enlarged empty state
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 shows the enlarged question, answer label, Change action and disabled submission together without visible overlap.
findings: Verify that the full question remains recoverable when a physical keyboard reduces the viewport.

screens.name: Custom answer — enlarged filled state
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 shows readable entered text and an enabled multiline Reveal my prediction button beneath the retained question.
findings: Extend the enlargement check to long answers that require scrolling inside the field.

screens.name: Custom answer — synthetic keyboard viewport
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 keeps the answer and submit button visible but does not show the question or answer label in the constrained capture.
findings: Keep a compact question summary visible or clearly recoverable above the keyboard-constrained answer field.

screens.name: Planning — loading and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 11 shows the processing stage, expected wait, credit reassurance and Cancel action with consistent transition composition.
findings: Verify announcement of stage changes and availability of cancellation during a prolonged request.

screens.name: Research — loading and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–12 distinguish research from planning through status text while retaining the same loading layout.
findings: Verify a clear timeout recovery state when the stated one-minute expectation is exceeded.

screens.name: Planning error — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 shows a clear failure heading, no-charge reassurance, primary retry and secondary question editing.
findings: Verify that retry preserves the question and announces the new request state.

screens.name: Prediction error — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 adds Review answers to the retry and edit recovery options without disguising the failure as a result.
findings: Verify that reviewing answers retains all responses through another prediction attempt.

screens.name: Sensitive planning redirect — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 13 shows support, another-question and edit actions plus explicit no-credit and no-memory reassurance.
findings: Give the support action greater prominence than the invitation to ask another question.

screens.name: Sensitive prediction redirect — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–14 preserve the same sensitive-redirect layout after prediction, and supplied evidence reports a real sensitive-flow drive.
findings: Make the support destination understandable before activation and verify its native accessibility.

screens.name: Reveal — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 12–13 make the forecast dominant and show uncertainty, explanation, check-back date and five follow-up actions.
findings: Group editing and review actions separately from sharing and reminders to reduce post-result choice density.

screens.name: Reveal — expanded explanation and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 12 shows an expanded explanation under a divider, with the long fixture paragraph continuing below the viewport.
findings: Structure long explanations into scannable context and assumptions sections without judging fixture content as model output.

screens.name: Check-in — unanswered and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 04–05 place the three outcome choices below the prediction and above the check-back date and share button.
findings: Give outcome choices a clearer selectable-control treatment before selection.

screens.name: Check-in — saved Not quite
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 shows matching inline saved status, a checkmarked Not quite choice and a confirmation notice; supplied evidence reports persistence after reload.
findings: Reduce the confirmation notice footprint so saved feedback does not compete with remaining actions.

screens.name: Check-in — saved Not yet
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 shows selected Not yet, explicit saved status and a waiting confirmation notice covering the lower portion of the screen.
findings: Keep the persistent inline status and make the additional notice less obstructive.

screens.name: Check-in — saved Yes
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 shows a checkmarked Yes choice and Came true saved status alongside a history confirmation notice.
findings: Confirm that selecting an outcome preserves an intentional scroll position and does not unexpectedly move the result header offscreen.

screens.name: History — empty and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows a clear empty-state message, direct Ask the Ball action and local-storage disclosure.
findings: Verify the text-only empty-state action has a full accessible touch target.

screens.name: History — populated and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 separates date, original question, forecast and check-back date within a borderless history row.
findings: Add a restrained cue that the history row can be opened.

screens.name: History — stress list
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows multiple consistent rows extending beneath the fixed navigation, with supplied layout checks covering responsive sizes.
findings: Verify that the last row can scroll completely above the fixed tab bar at enlarged text sizes.

screens.name: History — persisted outcome
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows a Came true checkmark on the saved row, and supplied evidence identifies actual storage behind the synthetic reading.
findings: Verify equivalent persisted row labels for Not quite and Not yet.

screens.name: Sky — offline samples and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 15 shows offline disclosure, Retry, checkmarked Love selection, a sample question and a fully visible primary action.
findings: Verify generous hit areas and a predictable assistive reading order for the spatially arranged stars.

screens.name: Circles — offline empty state
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 discloses the outage, offers Retry and visibly disables creation while explaining sharing boundaries.
findings: Clarify whether the disabled friends setting is unavailable because of age eligibility, the outage, or both.

screens.name: Plans — normal and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11 show checked yearly selection, billing cadence, savings, alternate packs and explicit simulated-payment labels.
findings: Verify selected-plan announcements and readable purchase-result feedback before enabling real billing.

screens.name: Plans — enlarged text
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 shows stacked enlarged prices and a fully visible subscription button, while alternate packs lie outside the captured view.
findings: Verify access to every alternate pack and test-mode explanation at native enlarged text sizes.

screens.name: Share — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 15 shows the portrait preview, explicit image download, story-video action and invitation privacy explanation; supplied evidence reports real PNG export.
findings: Make the distinction between a story video and a still story-card export explicit throughout the flow.

screens.name: Story — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 16 shows a large portrait card and Export story card button, but the supplied runtime summary establishes PNG export rather than video delivery.
findings: Align the export label with the actual delivered format and verify that format end to end.

screens.name: You — empty memory and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 16–17 distinguish plan, memory and preferences, with supplied evidence reporting wide keyboard-operable persistent switches.
findings: Consolidate the repeated See plans and View plans and credits entry points if they lead to the same destination.

screens.name: You — populated real memory
screens.evidence: Sheet 16 shows concrete remembered facts with Edit and Forget actions, and supplied evidence reports real-flow fact editing, forgetting and Undo.
findings: Ensure each repeated Edit and Forget control announces its associated fact.

screens.name: Settings — controls and keyboard focus
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 shows a full-row focus outline, and supplied controls evidence reports 342×52px targets with label, Space and Enter activation.
findings: Verify switch names, states and activation on VoiceOver and TalkBack.

screens.name: Settings — enlarged controls
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 shows enlarged preference labels and a selected large-text switch, while tab labels remain visibly small.
findings: Support enlarged navigation labels or demonstrate an equally readable native accessibility treatment.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: The sheets consistently use the illustrated orb as the hero, and supplied evidence reports sampled animation performance and stopped draws under reduced motion.
findings: Verify a clear accessible name when interactive and exclusion from the accessibility tree when decorative.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: The five-tab bar uses text, icons and selected underlines, but its labels remain small even in the enlarged settings capture.
findings: Increase label readability and verify native target sizes and selected-tab announcements.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Headers consistently pair a title or wordmark with a small daily balance, with captured states showing both zero and one remaining.
findings: Use “1 reading left today” where space permits so the balance is self-explanatory.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: Cream-filled buttons consistently dominate actions, accommodate enlarged wrapping and distinguish disabled custom-answer submission.
findings: Verify pressed, busy and disabled announcements across the shared button treatment.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Gold text actions recur throughout the app, with the reveal displaying several similarly weighted actions.
findings: Reduce simultaneous secondary actions and verify full touch targets around text-only labels.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Question screens show spacious divider-separated choices, and supplied evidence reports Space/Enter activation and focus transfer.
findings: Verify that immediate advancement and restored selections remain understandable with native assistive technology.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: The normal Ask captures show a labeled multiline field with a gold rectangular boundary and a second bottom rule.
findings: Simplify the doubled field border while retaining an unmistakable focus indicator.

components.name: Large-text input
components.evidence: Enlarged captures retain readable input and submission, but the synthetic keyboard capture omits visible question context.
findings: Preserve a recoverable question label and verify long-input editing with a physical keyboard viewport.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheet 14 shows distinct switch positions and a full-row focus ring, supported by reported target-size, activation and persistence checks.
findings: Complete native assistive checks for each switch’s label and current state.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheets 08–09 show both a successful fixture omen and a smaller unavailable state with concrete next steps.
findings: Verify longer omen content and unavailable guidance at native enlarged text sizes.

components.name: Sky stars and selected question
components.evidence: Sheet 15 ties a checkmarked Love star to the selected sample question and visible Ask this too button.
findings: Verify star hit areas, focus order and explicit selected-state announcements.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheet 05 combines offline recovery, privacy explanations and disabled creation and permission controls.
findings: Associate each disabled control with its specific reason rather than relying on surrounding copy.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheet 07 clearly separates date, question, forecast and outcome or check-back metadata.
findings: Expose each row as a clearly named openable item with its saved outcome included.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Normal and enlarged plan captures show selected yearly billing with a checkmark and explicit annual total beside the monthly equivalent.
findings: Verify that the entire option is selectable and its billing cadence is announced with its selected state.

components.name: Share preview
components.evidence: The small share preview and larger story card preserve forecast and disclaimer hierarchy, while the smaller preview makes supporting text difficult to inspect.
findings: Offer an accessible text equivalent and a way to inspect the export at readable size.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Voice and saved-outcome captures show explicit notices with Dismiss, while error screens provide contextual retry and editing.
findings: Shrink routine confirmation notices and verify that notices announce without obscuring or stealing focus from essential controls.

components.name: Typography system
components.evidence: The sheets consistently separate expressive serif headings from sans-serif controls, with small metadata and navigation labels remaining the weakest tier.
findings: Raise the smallest supporting-text sizes and ensure navigation participates in accessible text enlargement.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: Dark mist and restrained gold remain coherent across captures, with supplied evidence reporting sampled rendered contrast and reduced-motion behavior.
findings: Extend contrast and motion checks to physical devices and longer changing-background sequences.

limitations: All scores are provisional: this evaluation inspected the attached sheets and used the supplied runtime summary without independently executing or inspecting its artifacts.
A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall is 0.4A + 0.6F, normalized over applicable dimensions and rounded to one decimal.
The required schema provides no separate A, F or overall fields; the six dimension scores provide their calculation inputs.
Transition pairs show consistent visible composition but cannot establish uninterrupted motion, timing, focus behavior or absence of intermediate layout shifts.

Reported browser checks support browser behavior only; physical devices, native text enlargement, keyboard safe areas, VoiceOver/TalkBack, microphone hardware, haptics, real payments and OS share delivery remain unverified.
Synthetic readings, fixture explanations and simulated purchases establish layout or exercised UI states only, not predictive accuracy, semantic quality or production billing.
The synthetic keyboard capture does not visibly retain the question; the supplied contextual-retention claim needs reconciliation with that capture and a physical-device check.
The Story video entry and Export story card destination leave delivered media format uncertain; supplied evidence explicitly establishes PNG export.
No hard-gate failure is established by the available evidence, but unreachable controls and complete native accessibility cannot be ruled out from these captures.
The authorized A >=9 and F >=9 threshold for every screen and component is not met, and the evidence does not permit 9/10 certification.
topFixes: Complete physical-device and assistive-technology checks, especially immediate question advancement, keyboard-constrained forms and enlarged navigation.
Preserve question context in the constrained custom-answer viewport and verify long-answer editing and submission.
Increase small navigation and supporting-text readability while preserving the restrained visual hierarchy.
Align Story video and story-card export labels with the actual delivered format.
Reduce saved-notice obstruction and simplify the cluster of secondary reveal actions.
Prioritize support in sensitive redirects and clarify why each offline Circles control is disabled.
